specificity migrated. SHA aee72ed on m1/resolution (gate: align 177, interview 81, fixtures 110, scalafmtCheckAll clean, run as the last action before commit).

HOW MUCH THE NUMBER MOVES, as the bead requires: on the worked example the published figure goes 0.6103 -> 0.6583. 4.8 points, and in the flattering direction, which is the direction every one of these has moved so far.

WHY, concretely: the fixture has four localizable units whose source masses sum to 2.6292 - unequal, per AGENTS.md rule 4. Mean-of-ratios gave each of the four a 0.25 vote regardless of whether it held 0.9 of the mass or 0.02. The low-mass units were the poorly-localized ones, so equal voting dragged the average down; weighting by the mass the quantity is actually defined on lifts it.

The distinguishing assertion is on the conditioning mass, not on the value: A must read 2.6292 and not 4.0. That is what a unit count looks like when it is wearing a mass's clothes, and it is the assertion the compression mutation would have failed on its first test set. I also pinned both formulas as literals - the inequality "the two differ" survives any change that moves them together, so it proves less than it looks like it does.

ONE THING I ALMOST SHIPPED. My first version added specificityMass beside the existing specificity: Option[Double]. That is exactly the fidelity twin I removed one commit earlier, reintroduced by hand within the hour, because I had learned "remove the fidelity twin" as a fact about fidelity instead of as a rule about carriers. Caught on the compile, before the test run. The remaining eight fields go straight to carrier-only; I am not going to rediscover this on each one.

Mutations killed: (1) mean-of-ratios -> conditioning mass reads 4.0, fails; (2) value-present-when-A=0 -> two tests fail, including the unrankable-unit case in WorkedExampleSuite, so the abstention branch is defended by a real corpus path and not only by a synthetic one.

Process note, since it nearly cost the work: I restored a mutated file with `git checkout --` and wiped the uncommitted implementation with it. Recovered from a backup made before the first mutation. Mutation testing on uncommitted work needs that backup made first, every time - `git checkout` is not an undo when the thing you want back was never staged.

Pending gate now: c1049f2, e538a09, 2adfff2, aee72ed. Next: the remaining eight fields, unless you want the queue drained first.
